info.description:
# Swarnay API

Generated from the running server on 2026-10-21.
355 endpoints.

## Start here

1. Set `baseUrl` — it defaults to the deployed backend.
2. **Super admin work:** run `Platform Operator → POST platform/auth/login`.
   The token is saved automatically into `platformToken`.
3. **Shop staff work:** run `Settings → POST auth/login` with a `tenantCode`.
   That token is saved into `token`, and the branch into `branchId`.

Every other request picks the right token up by itself.

## Why two logins

A super admin has no tenant, so they sign in with just email and password.
Shop staff belong to one business, so they also send `tenantCode` — that is
what tells the server which shop `rajesh@gmail.com` works at.

## Variables

- `baseUrl` — the server
- `platformToken` / `token` — filled in by the two logins
- `tenantId`, `branchId`, `id` — fill these in as you go
- `today`, `nowIso` — set automatically before each request

Give a count; each demo is a complete business made through the same services as a real one: one to three branches, an owner, a branch admin per branch, two to four staff roles named and given random permissions, one or two staff per branch, and sample data in every module — rates, items, formulas, customers, suppliers, karigars, purchases, tagged stock, bills, receipts, an approval memo, orders, old gold, scheme members with their collections, girvi loans and expenses.

Codes are `demo-xxxxx` and every login in a demo shares one password, shown only by the job. No password change is asked for at first sign-in.

A demo takes tens of seconds, so this answers 202 at once with a job; poll `GET /api/platform/demo-tenants/jobs/:id`. Demos are made one at a time across the platform. A demo whose business, people or masters cannot be made is removed again and listed under `failures`.

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.create`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `202` — Started. Poll the job.
- `400` — A count below 1 or above the limit.

Only the operator who started the job can read it, because it carries the passwords. Finished jobs are kept for an hour and then forgotten — copy the logins before that.

Jobs live in the memory of the server that started them: a restart forgets them, and a demo being made at that moment is left half-made (delete it from its tenant page).

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.create`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `200` — The job.
- `404` — No such job, someone else’s, or more than an hour old.

For a count typed by mistake. The demo being made is finished — cutting it off would leave half a business to delete — and no further demo is started. Demos already made stay; delete them from their tenant pages if they are not wanted. Stopping a finished job changes nothing.

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.create`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `200` — The job, with `stopped: true`.
- `404` — No such job, someone else’s, or more than an hour old.

Each kind lists its fields (key, label, type, required, the closed options of a list, what a lookup field names), the options a batch can take with their defaults, and whether importing it posts to the books. The console builds its picker, matching screen and "Download sample" files from this. Kinds are in the order a shop is best brought over in: masters, stock, balances, running accounts.

What the role builder ticks. Built from the live routes, so it cannot offer a switch the API does not enforce — if a permission is here, granting it genuinely grants something.

`module` is the top level (Billing, Stock). `groups` are the areas within it, and a group whose key equals the module is that module’s own actions rather than a sub-area. `wildcard` on each level is the string to grant for "all of this".

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.view`

One platform role, holding everything. Inside a business there are three kinds: `owner`, `admin` and `staff`. Only the first two are seeded — staff roles are named and given their permissions per business, because one shop’s accountant is not another’s. `isBranchAdmin` marks the role limited to one holder per branch.

This is the record a tenant is shown when they ask who looked at their data. `action_count` is how many audited changes were made inside the window.

**Permission:** `platform.support.view`

The only way a platform role reaches business data. Returns a `token` to send as `Authorization: Bearer` against ordinary tenant endpoints — it is shown once and stored only as a hash, so a lost token means opening a new session.

Read-only unless `canWrite` is set. The session row is checked on every request, so ending it locks the operator out at once rather than when the token would have expired. Every action inside the window is tagged with the session in the tenant’s own audit log.

**Permission:** `platform.support.create`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `201` — Session opened.
- `403` — Write access asked for without `platform.support.write`.
- `404` — No such tenant.

request.description:
List every tenant

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.view`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `200` — Tenants with user and branch counts.

One call sets up everything a business needs to start: the tenant, its chart of accounts, purities, numbering series, the five roles, the head user (Admin) and the first branch with its stock locations. A half-created tenant is worse than none, so this does the lot.

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.create`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `201` — Tenant ready to use.
- `400` — Invalid code or a password under 8 characters.
- `409` — That tenant code is taken.

Only for demos (`is_demo`). A real business is never deleted — suspend or close it instead, which keeps its records. Everything the demo held goes: users, branches, stock, bills, ledgers. The console’s own audit log keeps its entries about it.

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.update`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `204` — Deleted.
- `404` — No such tenant.
- `422` — `tenant_not_demo` — a real business cannot be deleted.

The staff list is included only for a role holding `platform.users.view`. A Billing Admin can see the business and its licences without seeing who works there.

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.view`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `200` — Everything the tenant detail screen needs.
- `404` — No such tenant.

Setting `status` to `suspended` blocks every user of that tenant from signing in. Their data is untouched.

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.update`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `200` — Updated.
- `404` — No such tenant.

Creates the branch together with its stock locations and its own document numbering series — without those the first invoice at that branch would fail.

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.update`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `201` — Branch created, with locations and numbering.
- `409` — That branch code already exists in this tenant.

For the value panel: which purity "22CT" is, which ledger "Cash A/c" is, which customer a name means. Short lists come whole; customers, items and karigars are searched (`search`) and capped at 200.

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.view`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `200` — Choices.

Newest first, with counts. `progress` says, kind by kind, how many records have been brought over (undone imports not counted) — the console’s checklist.

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.view`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `200` — Imports.
- `404` — No such business.

Returns the batch with `mapping` already suggested from the headings (Customer Name, Mob No., Gr Wt, Tunch… are recognised), ready for the rows. Headings must be present and different from each other.

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.update`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `201` — Created, with suggested matching.
- `400` — Unknown kind, missing or repeated headings, or a bad option.
- `404` — No such business.

For a file staged by mistake. An import with rows brought in is undone instead, which keeps its record.

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.update`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `204` — Deleted.
- `422` — `import_locked`: rows were imported — undo it instead.

Poll this while a job runs (`running`). `statusCounts` counts rows by status; `sample` is the first five rows as they arrived, for the matching screen.

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.view`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `200` — The batch.
- `404` — No such business or import.

`mapping` replaces the whole matching: field → { column } or { constant }, with `unit` for weights and `format` for dates. `valueMap` is field → { value as written in the file → what it means here } — a record id from GET …/import-choices for a lookup field, or the option’s value for a list. Changing any of these sends the batch back to draft: check it again before importing. Once rows are imported they are fixed (422 `import_locked`).

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.update`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `200` — Updated.
- `400` — A field, column, unit or option that does not exist.
- `422` — `import_locked` once rows are imported; `import_busy` while a job runs.

Imports every row the check passed, in chunks; each row is checked once more as it goes in. Masters are added or updated, stock is tagged, balances and running accounts are posted to the books dated the cut-over day. Rows with errors are only left out when `leaveOutInvalid` says so. Runs in the background: answers 202, poll the batch. Calling it again on an import that stopped or was cut short carries on from where it got to.

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.update`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `202` — Importing.
- `422` — `import_not_ready` (check first), `import_has_errors` (fix or leave out), `import_empty`, `import_busy`.

`status`: one or more of pending, valid, invalid, skipped, imported, failed, undone, comma-separated. `level=warning` keeps rows with a warning. `search` looks in the cells, the label and the messages.

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.view`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `200` — Rows in file order.

Up to 1000 rows a call, each an object keyed by the file’s headings. `firstRow` is the file row of rows[0], so every message points at a row the shop can find. Sending a range again replaces it, so a retried call never doubles rows. Only before the import starts.

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.update`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `200` — Stored.
- `422` — `import_locked` once the import has started; `import_too_large` past 200,000 rows.

`data` holds only the cells to change, by heading. `skip: true` leaves the row out of the import. The file needs checking again afterwards.

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.update`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `200` — The row, waiting to be checked.
- `422` — `row_imported`: the row is in already.

What has gone in stays. The rest stays waiting: import again to carry on, or undo what went in.

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.update`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `200` — Stopping.
- `422` — `import_not_running`.

Masters the import added are removed unless something has used them since (they stay, with the reason); masters it changed get their old values back, except fields changed again since. Stock, balances, scheme members and loans come out together or not at all: every opening voucher is reversed on its own date, pieces are written off with their tag numbers freed, scheme accounts and loans are cancelled with their numbers freed. Refused with 422 `import_in_use` when that would undo something that happened since (a piece sold, a collection taken, a loan repaid).

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.update`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `202` — Undoing.
- `422` — `import_not_imported`, `import_in_use`, `import_busy`.

Reads every row through the matching against the shop as it is now: what each would do (add, update, leave), what is wrong, which values could not be placed (`validation.unknown`), what would be created on the way (`validation.willCreate`) and totals to compare with the old software (`validation.totals`). Runs in the background: answers 202, poll the batch.

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.update`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `202` — Checking.
- `422` — `import_busy`, `import_empty` or `import_locked`.

Grant, revoke, or move a module between included / purchased / trial. A module whose trial or term has lapsed still appears in the tenant’s dock, but locked — so they can see what they are missing rather than having it silently vanish.

`enabled: false` switches the module off: it leaves the tenant’s dock and every endpoint belonging to it answers 403 `module_disabled`, for staff and support sessions alike. `disabledSubmodules` does the same for single sub-modules that have permissions of their own (e.g. `pos.purchase`) — see `enforced` on `GET /api/platform/modules`. Other sub-module keys are accepted but nothing checks them yet. Data is never touched, so switching back on restores everything as it was.

Master Data, Settings and SaaS Admin are `required` in the catalog and cannot be switched off.

**Permission:** `platform.entitlement.update`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `200` — Entitlement updated.
- `400` — A sub-module key that does not belong to this module.
- `403` — Not a super admin.
- `404` — No such tenant, or no such module.
- `422` — `module_required` — this module cannot be switched off.

Owner and Branch Admin are seeded and fixed. Everything else is a staff role you named and gave permissions to. `user_count` is how many people hold each.

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.view`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `200` — Roles with their permissions.

The code is derived from the name. Permissions must come from `GET /api/platform/permission-tree` — anything else is refused, so a role cannot be given a right that nothing enforces.

Only staff roles can be created: Owner and Branch Admin already exist and are fixed.

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.update`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `201` — Created.
- `400` — An unknown permission, or a reserved name.
- `409` — This business already has a role with that name.

Delete a staff role nobody holds

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.update`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `204` — Deleted.
- `422` — Still held by somebody, or a fixed role.

Send the complete permission list, not a delta. Everyone holding the role is signed back in against the new list immediately rather than at token expiry.

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.update`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `200` — Updated.
- `404` — No such role.
- `422` — Owner and Branch Admin are fixed.

The passcode itself is never returned — only whether one is set. Includes how many vault unlocks are open right now and who is locked out.

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.view`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `200` — Settings.
- `404` — No such tenant.

Points are normalised over the 404 artwork (x 0.07–0.93, y 0.10–0.90) and at least 96 artwork units apart. Switching it on needs a valid path and three points. Every save ends any open private-entry grant.

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.update`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `200` — Saved.
- `400` — Path or points not usable.
- `409` — `conflict` — changed by someone else since it was loaded.

Omit `userId` to clear everyone in this business.

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.update`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `200` — How many were cleared.

Send the whole setting with the `revision` you loaded; a stale revision gets 409. Leave `passcode` out to keep the current one. Every save locks the vault for everyone who had it open, and a new passcode clears old wrong-try lockouts.

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.update`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `200` — Saved.
- `400` — Passcode under 6 characters, or no role chosen.
- `409` — `conflict` — changed by someone else since it was loaded.
- `422` — `vault_passcode_required` — switched on with no passcode set.

Only you can do this — nobody inside the business can create users. Give `branchId` to place the person at one branch; leave it out and they cover all branches. A branch has exactly one admin, so creating a second one for the same branch is refused with `409` naming whoever already holds the slot.

**Permission:** `platform.users.create`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `201` — User created.
- `409` — Email already used here, or that branch already has an admin.

Moving someone to `admin`, or moving an existing admin to another branch, is refused if that branch already has one. The only admin in a business cannot be deactivated — the shop would be left with nobody able to run it.

Name and contact editing lives here because it has no tenant-side equivalent: a shop cannot edit its own staff, so without this a misspelled name could never be corrected.

**Permission:** `platform.users.update`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `200` — Updated.
- `409` — That branch already has an admin.
- `422` — Would leave the business with no admin.

The recovery path for a locked-out shop, and the only one: staff are yours to manage, so the tenant-side reset no longer exists. The password is returned once and never stored in readable form. They are signed out everywhere and must set a new password at next sign-in.

**Permission:** `platform.users.reset_password`
**Auth:** super admin token

**Responses**
- `200` — Reset.
- `404` — No such user.

Every module the platform offers. Used by the SaaS admin screen when provisioning.

**Permission:** `platform.tenants.view`
**Auth:** shop staff token

**Responses**
- `200` — All modules.

request.description:
Whether the vault is on for this business and whether the signed-in person may unlock it. No secret is returned. When `canUnlock` is false, show `message` instead of the passcode box.

**Permission:** `settings.vault.unlock`
**Auth:** shop staff token

**Responses**

Lock private figures now

**Permission:** `settings.vault.unlock`
**Auth:** shop staff token

**Responses**
- `204` — Locked.

Send the token from unlock. Returns its expiry, or `null` once it has expired or been ended for any reason — then lock the screen.

**Permission:** `settings.vault.unlock`
**Auth:** shop staff token

**Responses**
- `200` — Still unlocked, or null.

Checks the passcode against the hash the super admin set. Five wrong tries lock that person out for 15 minutes. The token is valid for the configured minutes, and stops working early if the vault is switched off or re-configured, or the person’s password or role changes.

**Permission:** `settings.vault.unlock`
**Auth:** shop staff token

**Responses**
- `200` — Unlocked.
- `403` — `vault_not_allowed` — this person’s role may not unlock.
- `422` — `vault_passcode_invalid` (wrong passcode, message says tries left) or `vault_disabled`.
- `429` — `vault_locked` — too many wrong passcodes; or `rate_limited` from one network.

Each entry carries `value` (what applies now) and `source` (whether that came from a branch override, a tenant override, or the built-in default). Grouped by `group` so the settings screen can render tabs directly.

**Permission:** `settings.config.view`
**Auth:** shop staff token

**Responses**
- `200` — Settings, grouped.

Validated against the setting’s declared type. Settings marked `sensitive` change how past numbers are interpreted — warn before saving those.

**Permission:** `settings.config.update`
**Auth:** shop staff token

**Responses**
- `200` — Saved.
- `400` — Unknown key, or the value failed its type check.

Reference only. Roles are fixed in code, so nothing here can be assigned or combined into a new role from inside a business.

**Permission:** `settings.roles.view`
**Auth:** shop staff token

**Responses**

Fixed in code and seeded per business. A shop can see what each role can do; only the super admin decides who holds one.

**Permission:** `settings.roles.view`

**Responses**
- `200` — Roles.

**Permission:** `settings.theme.view`

- `200` — Theme preset and CSS variable overrides.

Preset keys match the frontend theme ids exactly.

**Permission:** `settings.theme.update`
**Auth:** shop staff token

**Responses**
- `200` — Saved.

Staff are created, named and given their access by the super admin. From inside the business the list is read-only, apart from switching someone off — see `POST /api/settings/users/:id/status`.

**Permission:** `settings.users.view`
**Auth:** shop staff token

**Responses**
- `200` — Staff.

The one change a business may make to its own people, because somebody leaving at short notice should not wait on us. Deactivating signs them out everywhere immediately.

Everything else about a staff member — creating them, their name, their role, what it reaches — stays with the super admin. An owner cannot be deactivated here, and nobody can switch off their own account.

**Permission:** `settings.users.status`
**Auth:** shop staff token

**Responses**
- `204` — Saved.
- `404` — No such person.
- `422` — Your own account, or the business owner.
